The Prince-Bishopric of Montenegro was the state of the Orthodox bishops of Cetinje, who ruled the mountain clans of Montenegro from 1696 to 1852. The office passed within the Petrović-Njegoš family, from uncle to nephew, since bishops could not marry.

Montenegro lay inside the claims of the Ottoman Empire but its rocky heartland was never fully held. The bishops led the clans in war, made peace between feuding families and sought help from Russia, whose tsars sent money from the time of Peter the Great. Petar II built the first state offices. In 1852 Danilo I gave up the church office and made himself a secular prince.
